rationale:
Decision: split into two independent children. The selected statement is the conjunction of two separate classical differentiation theorems for two different weighted measures:
- (L) is the Lebesgue-point property of g for θ₁·H⌞M₁ (Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation).
- (D) is the Besicovitch density of A in θ₂·H⌞M₂.
Neither part uses the other. The supplied proof only interleaves them, using ν₁ for (L) and ν₂ for (D). Each child carries the matching steps of the supplied proof, specialized to one weight (M, θ).

Both children are stated generically:
- They hold for any measure μ on ℝ^P, because the supplied proof uses no property of H.
- (L) takes a general integrand f with θf ∈ L¹(μ⌞(M ∩ B̄_r(y))).
- (D) takes an arbitrary null-measurable E ⊆ M.
In these forms they are reusable lemmas. Weighted Lebesgue-point obligations of this kind recur in this DAG, for example ind_ab_weighted_lebesgue_point in the integrality branch (different frozen type, no name clash). The children have no sibling dependencies and can run in parallel.

weighted_lebesgue_point repeats inline the three-line closed-ball Lebesgue differentiation argument: VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt. As a result, no grandchild relies on the uncle declaration fiw_tl_ald_closedBall_lebesgue_point. Neither child restates another DAG node.

Residual proof of the selected node (assembly, checked in Lean):
1. A := M₁ ∩ M₂ is H-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.inter).
2. For every z, θ₁(z)·g(z) = A.indicator θ₂ (z):
   - if z ∈ A, then θ₁(z)·(θ₂(z)/θ₁(z)) = θ₂(z) by mul_div_cancel₀, since θ₁(z) > 0;
   - otherwise both sides are 0.
   By integrableOn_indicator_iff (A is null-measurable), θ₁·g is H-integrable on M₁ ∩ B̄_r(y) iff θ₂ is H-integrable on A ∩ (M₁ ∩ B̄_r(y)). That set is contained in M₂ ∩ B̄_r(y), so this follows from IntegrableOn.mono_set.
3. Apply weighted_lebesgue_point with (μ, M, θ, f) := (H, M₁, θ₁, g). It gives the limit with ‖g(z) − g(x)‖ₑ for H⌞(M₁ ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. x. Since M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ M₁ ∩ B_r(y), the same holds for H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
4. Apply weighted_density_point with (μ, M, E, θ) := (H, M₂, A, θ₂), using A ⊆ M₂ (Set.inter_subset_right). This yields (D) verbatim, because E ∩ ball y r and E ∩ closedBall x s instantiate to M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ ball y r and M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ closedBall x s.
5. For H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. x we have x ∈ A (ae_restrict_mem₀), so g(x) = θ₂(x)/θ₁(x) (Set.indicator_of_mem). This turns step 3 into (L). Combine steps 3–5 with filter_upwards.

Background: these are the Besicovitch–Lebesgue differentiation theorems for Radon measures on ℝ^P (standard, e.g. Evans–Gariepy, Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions, §1.6–1.7), which Mathlib provides as Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div and VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div.

subproblems.title: Weighted Lebesgue points of f for θ·μ⌞M along closed balls, a.e. on M ∩ B_r(y)
subproblems.statement:
Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Borel σ-algebra). Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be μ-null-measurable, and let θ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ > 0 on M. Let y ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ, and suppose θ and θ·f are both μ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y). Then for μ⌞(M ∩ B_r(y))-almost every x, as s → 0⁺ (quotient in [0, ∞]):
(∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ(z))·‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dμ(z)) / (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ(z)) dμ(z)) → 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ f : Eucl P → ℝ) (y : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M μ → (∀ z ∈ M, 0 < θ z) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall y r) μ → IntegrableOn (fun z => θ z * f z) (M ∩ closedBall y r) μ → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict (M ∩ ball y r)), Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in M ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ z) * ‖f z - f x‖ₑ ∂μ) / (∫⁻ z in M ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ z) ∂μ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 3(a), 4, 5(a) and 6(i)–(ii) of the parent-supplied proof of fiw_tl_ald_local_differentiation. They are specialized to one weight (M, θ) and a general integrand f (the parent's g), with H replaced by an arbitrary measure μ; that proof uses no property of H. The closed-ball Lebesgue differentiation step is derived directly from Mathlib in step 5. It is the same argument as the sibling node closed_ball_lebesgue_point, repeated here so that this proof is self-contained.

Notation: K := B̄_r(y) = closedBall y r, S := M ∩ K, B_s := B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s, t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t, ν := (μ⌞S).withDensity (z ↦ θ(z)⁺) and λ := μ⌞(M ∩ B_r(y)).

1. Null-measurability. K is closed, hence measurable, so S is μ-null-measurable. Therefore μ⌞S-a.e. z lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀). Likewise M ∩ B_r(y) is μ-null-measurable, since open balls are measurable.

2. Finiteness. ν(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_S θ⁺ dμ ≤ ∫⁻_S ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞, because θ is μ-integrable on S. Formally, isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal applied to the HasFiniteIntegral part of IntegrableOn θ S μ gives IsFiniteMeasure ν. Hence ν is s-finite and locally finite.

3. Reverse absolute continuity. θ is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞S (part of its integrability), so θ⁺ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal). For μ⌞S-a.e. z we have z ∈ M, so θ(z) > 0 and θ(z)⁺ ≠ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). By withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', μ⌞S ≪ ν.

4. f ∈ L¹(ν).
(a) ENNReal.ofReal t is by definition the coercion of t.toNNReal, so ν = (μ⌞S).withDensity (z ↦ ↑(θ(z).toNNReal)). The function z ↦ θ(z).toNNReal is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S (AEMeasurable.real_toNNReal).
(b) By integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul₀, f is ν-integrable iff z ↦ θ(z).toNNReal • f(z) is μ⌞S-integrable.
(c) For μ⌞S-a.e. z we have θ(z) > 0, hence θ(z).toNNReal • f(z) = θ(z)·f(z) (NNReal.smul_def, Real.coe_toNNReal, smul_eq_mul).
(d) z ↦ θ(z)·f(z) is μ⌞S-integrable by hypothesis. By (c) and Integrable.congr, z ↦ θ(z).toNNReal • f(z) is μ⌞S-integrable, so f is ν-integrable by (b).
(e) In particular f is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν, hence for μ⌞S by step 3 (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).

5. Lebesgue differentiation for ν along closed balls.
(a) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space. So it is a second-countable metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, and it has the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering).
(b) Since ν is s-finite, Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν is a Vitali family for ν.
(c) Because f ∈ L¹(ν), f is locally integrable for ν (Integrable.locallyIntegrable), and ν is locally finite. VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div then gives, for ν-a.e. x: (∫⁻_a ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(a) → 0 as a → x along (Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν).filterAt x.
(d) By Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν x, s ↦ B_s tends to that filter as s → 0⁺. Composing (Tendsto.comp) gives, for ν-a.e. x: Q(s) := (∫⁻_{B_s} ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(B_s) → 0 as s → 0⁺.

6. Transfer to λ. M ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ S because ball y r ⊆ closedBall y r. So λ ≤ μ⌞S (Measure.restrict_mono), and hence λ ≪ μ⌞S ≪ ν (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_of_le, step 3, AbsolutelyContinuous.trans). By AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le, the conclusion of step 5 holds for λ-a.e. x. Also, by step 1 and ae_restrict_mem₀, x ∈ M ∩ B_r(y) for λ-a.e. x. Fix x with both properties (filter_upwards). It remains to prove the stated limit at x.

7. Identification on small balls. Since x ∈ B_r(y), ρ := r − dist(x, y) > 0, and (0, ρ) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). For s ∈ (0, ρ) we have s + dist(x, y) ≤ r. So B_s ⊆ K (closedBall_subset_closedBall'), and therefore B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s. The ball B_s is measurable.
(i) ∫⁻_{B_s} ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dν(z) = ∫⁻_{B_s} θ(z)⁺·‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ d(μ⌞S)(z) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_s} θ(z)⁺·‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ dμ(z).
- The first equality is setLIntegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀. Its hypotheses hold: θ⁺ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S by step 3, and z ↦ ‖f(z) − f(x)‖ₑ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S by step 4(e) (AEStronglyMeasurable.sub with a constant, then .enorm).
- The second equality is Measure.restrict_restrict together with B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s.
(ii) ν(B_s) = ∫⁻_{B_s} θ⁺ d(μ⌞S) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_s} θ⁺ dμ, by withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict and B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s.
Hence for every s ∈ (0, ρ), Q(s) equals the quotient in the statement. The two functions of s therefore agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and Tendsto.congr' transfers the limit 0 of step 5 to the stated quotient. This holds for λ-almost every x, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν := (μ⌞(M∩K)).withDensity θ⁺ with K = B̄_r(y) is finite, because θ ∈ L¹(μ⌞(M∩K)) (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal). Also μ⌞(M∩K) ≪ ν, because θ > 0 on M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous').
f ∈ L¹(ν): integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul₀ reduces this to θ·f ∈ L¹(μ⌞(M∩K)), since θ.toNNReal•f = θf a.e. Hence f is also AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞(M∩K) (mono_ac).
Lebesgue differentiation for ν along closed balls: VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν x.
Transfer: λ = μ⌞(M ∩ B_r(y)) ≤ μ⌞(M∩K) ≪ ν, so the limit holds λ-a.e. (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). Also x ∈ M ∩ B_r(y) λ-a.e.

For 0 < s < r − dist(x, y), B̄_s(x) ⊆ K, so the ν-quotient equals the μ-quotient (setLIntegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀, withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). Conclude by Tendsto.congr'.

subproblems.title: Besicovitch density of E ⊆ M for θ·μ⌞M along closed balls, a.e. on E ∩ B_r(y)
subproblems.statement:
Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Borel σ-algebra). Let M, E ⊆ ℝ^P be μ-null-measurable with E ⊆ M, and let θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ > 0 on M. Let y ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ, and suppose θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y). Then for μ⌞(E ∩ B_r(y))-almost every x, as s → 0⁺ (quotient in [0, ∞]):
(∫⁻_{E∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ(z)) dμ(z)) / (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ(z)) dμ(z)) → 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (M E : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (y : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M μ → NullMeasurableSet E μ → E ⊆ M → (∀ z ∈ M, 0 < θ z) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall y r) μ → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict (E ∩ ball y r)), Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in E ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ z) ∂μ) / (∫⁻ z in M ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ z) ∂μ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 3(b), 5(b), 6(i) and 6(iii) of the parent-supplied proof of fiw_tl_ald_local_differentiation. They are specialized to one weight (M, θ) (the parent's (M₂, θ₂)) and a subset E ⊆ M (the parent's A = M₁ ∩ M₂), with H replaced by an arbitrary measure μ; that proof uses no property of H.

Notation: K := B̄_r(y) = closedBall y r, S := M ∩ K, B_s := B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s, t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t, ν := (μ⌞S).withDensity (z ↦ θ(z)⁺) and λ := μ⌞(E ∩ B_r(y)).

1. Null-measurability. K is closed, hence measurable, so S is μ-null-measurable, and μ⌞S-a.e. z lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀). E ∩ B_r(y) is μ-null-measurable, since open balls are measurable. E is null-measurable for μ⌞S (NullMeasurableSet.mono with Measure.restrict_le_self). Hence so is E ∩ B_s for every s, since closed balls are measurable.

2. Finiteness. ν(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_S θ⁺ dμ ≤ ∫⁻_S ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞, because θ is μ-integrable on S. Formally, isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal applied to the HasFiniteIntegral part of the hypothesis gives IsFiniteMeasure ν. So ν is locally finite.

3. Reverse absolute continuity. θ⁺ is AEMeasurable for μ⌞S: take the AEStronglyMeasurable part of the integrability of θ and apply AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal. For μ⌞S-a.e. z we have z ∈ M, so θ(z) > 0 and θ(z)⁺ ≠ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). By withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', μ⌞S ≪ ν.

4. Absolute continuity of λ with respect to ν⌞E.
(a) By step 1 and Measure.restrict_restrict₀, (μ⌞S)⌞E = μ⌞(E ∩ S).
(b) Since E ⊆ M and ball y r ⊆ closedBall y r, we have E ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ E ∩ S. So λ ≤ (μ⌞S)⌞E (Measure.restrict_mono).
(c) Restricting step 3 to E (AbsolutelyContinuous.restrict) gives (μ⌞S)⌞E ≪ ν⌞E.
(d) Hence λ ≪ ν⌞E (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_of_le and AbsolutelyContinuous.trans).

5. Besicovitch density theorem. ℝ^P is a second-countable metric space with its Borel σ-algebra and the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering for finite-dimensional normed spaces), and ν is locally finite by step 2. Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div ν E holds for an arbitrary set E. It gives: for ν⌞E-a.e. x, Q(s) := ν(E ∩ B_s) / ν(B_s) → 1 as s → 0⁺. By step 4 and AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le, this holds for λ-a.e. x. Also λ-a.e. x lies in E ∩ B_r(y) (ae_restrict_mem₀, step 1). Fix x with both properties (filter_upwards).

6. Identification on small balls. Since x ∈ B_r(y), ρ := r − dist(x, y) > 0, and (0, ρ) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). For s ∈ (0, ρ) we have s + dist(x, y) ≤ r, so B_s ⊆ K (closedBall_subset_closedBall').
(i) E ∩ B_s is null-measurable for μ⌞S by step 1. So withDensity_apply₀ and Measure.restrict_restrict₀ give ν(E ∩ B_s) = ∫⁻_{E∩B_s} θ⁺ d(μ⌞S) = ∫⁻_{(E∩B_s)∩S} θ⁺ dμ. Moreover (E ∩ B_s) ∩ S = E ∩ B_s, because E ⊆ M and B_s ⊆ K. So ν(E ∩ B_s) = ∫⁻_{E∩B_s} θ⁺ dμ.
(ii) B_s is measurable, so withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict give ν(B_s) = ∫⁻_{B_s∩S} θ⁺ dμ. Moreover B_s ∩ S = M ∩ B_s, because B_s ⊆ K. So ν(B_s) = ∫⁻_{M∩B_s} θ⁺ dμ.
Thus Q(s) equals the quotient in the statement for every s ∈ (0, ρ). The two functions of s agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and Tendsto.congr' transfers the limit 1 from step 5 to the stated quotient. This holds for λ-almost every x, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν := (μ⌞(M∩K)).withDensity θ⁺ with K = B̄_r(y) is finite, because θ ∈ L¹(μ⌞(M∩K)). Also μ⌞(M∩K) ≪ ν, because θ > 0 on M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous').
λ = μ⌞(E ∩ B_r(y)) ≤ (μ⌞(M∩K))⌞E = μ⌞(E ∩ (M∩K)) ≪ ν⌞E, using E ⊆ M, Measure.restrict_restrict₀ and AbsolutelyContinuous.restrict.
Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div ν E: ν(E ∩ B̄_s(x))/ν(B̄_s(x)) → 1 for ν⌞E-a.e. x, hence λ-a.e. Also x ∈ E ∩ B_r(y) λ-a.e.

For 0 < s < r − dist(x, y), B̄_s(x) ⊆ K, so ν(E ∩ B̄_s(x)) = ∫⁻_{E∩B̄_s(x)} θ⁺ dμ and ν(B̄_s(x)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ⁺ dμ (withDensity_apply₀ / withDensity_apply with restrict_restrict₀ / restrict_restrict). Conclude by Tendsto.congr'.
